gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's Apex 300 stack accepts 150–500 V rooftop-style strings only through the separate $699 SolarX 4K controller (up to 4 kW, stepped down to below 60 V), so the 8,294.4 Wh kits' own 400 W or 1,000 W of portable panels are what sets the refill time: 20.7 or 8.3 hours of rated sun.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts' 240 V solar-input page (cited), StormWatts' same-panel-watts kit page, Solar Waypoint (cited) and EnergySage (cited). StormWatts already gives per-port volt/amp windows for the Jackery 5000 Plus, Anker S5000, DELTA Pro 3 and F3800 Plus, the Jackery cap of about 438 W per SolarSaga 500 X, and the Apex 300's two native 1,200 W inputs. EnergySage already says the Apex 300 takes 2,400 W, with more through the SolarX 4K. None of them gives the SolarX 4K's 150–500 V window or its $699 price, BLUETTI's no-panel SolarX bundle at $4,498, or refill hours for a roughly 10 kWh kit from its own panels. I could not open BLUETTI's manual for the Apex 300's native port window (the detail that would have rated 2–3), so the new part is partial.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. Among the kits we link, only the two Apex 300 + 2× B300K kits fall within 20% of 10 kWh, and the 2× 500 W version is the one to name: 8.3 rated sun-hours against 20.7 for the 2× 200 W version. Both are pre-orders dispatching late January 2027, so no linked kit in the size range ships now. A shopper who wants a one-day refill needs about 2,000 W or more of panels. That fits inside the 2,400 W native limit StormWatts and EnergySage report, but a rooftop string of 150–500 V needs the $699 SolarX 4K, and BLUETTI's bundle with it has no panels. The Jackery 10 kWh Home Kit shown by ChatGPT has the same shortfall: its two 500 W panels deliver about 876 W by StormWatts' port figures, or 11.5 hours for 10.08 kWh.
